cards.title: Re-assessing never updates the dashboard (primary newest-wins)
cards.summary: DONE pending review (committed to master). Root-caused the dashboard-pinning bug found while live-smoking MV-14: partial-unique index assessments_primary_idx = UNIQUE(owner) WHERE is_primary allows one primary per owner; the dashboard reads the primary one; but claimAndBootstrapProfile ran a single unconditional promote (update is_primary=true .eq(id).is(is_primary,false)) and DISCARDED the returned {error}. On the 2nd+ claim the owner already has a primary, so the promote violated the index, the error was swallowed, the new row stayed is_primary=false, and the dashboard stayed pinned to the first assessment ever claimed (confirmed live: owner ece83f09 has 16 assessments, only the oldest is primary). Fix A (newest-wins): demote-then-promote as TWO sequential app-layer updates (business logic in Next.js, NOT a Postgres RPC — Codex suggested an RPC, overruled): (1) is_primary=false where owner=userId and is_primary=true, (2) is_primary=true where id=assessmentId; after the demote the owner has no primary so the promote can't trip the index. Both {error} results are now read + structured-logged ([claim] demote/promote ... failed) — no longer swallowed; misleading comment fixed; MV-14 lead-insert unchanged. Design call: LOG not throw (auth/callback has no try/catch — throwing would 500 an already-claimed user); residual demote-ok/promote-fail leaves a momentary no-primary state (logged), which MV-17 removes for the common path. No DB schema/scoring/golden change; F16 untouched. Gate green: typecheck/lint, full suite 1270/1270 (+2 TDD: newest-wins order+filters; failed-promote-is-logged). FOUNDER-OWED: live smoke (2nd assessment on an existing account → dashboard shows the new result; new row is_primary=true, old flipped false); existing pinned rows self-heal on next claim only (retro fix = prod write, founder-gated). Dossier: cards/MV-16-primary-assessment-newest-wins.md.

cards.title: Anonymous persist-miss: recover in place, not a dead 'Run it again'
cards.summary: Consultancy-replacement / journey-reliability (primary C; Codex gpt-5.5 + Claude agreed). On an anonymous persist miss (POST /api/assess returns 200 with id:null — the DB insert failed), BOTH results CTAs (ConversionPrompt near the verdict + the ConversionPaths card at the bottom) linked to /assess?new=1, which wiped the wizard + results sessionStorage and dumped the student back to a BLANK 9-step wizard — and if the DB was still down it looped forever (a guaranteed bounce to a consultancy). But the full profile + computed payload are already in memory; only the server save failed. FIX (TDD): thread an in-place onRetrySave (+ retryingSave) from AssessFlow.save() through Results into both CTAs; the dead /assess?new=1 link becomes a 'Try saving again' button that re-POSTs the same answers (no wizard reset, no data loss), and on success the prompt flips to the real 'Continue with Google' conversion. Honest copy, no false 3-day-expiry promise. Other /assess?new=1 links (interstitial, unsupported-corridor notice, marketing) left untouched — those are legit fresh starts. Files: components/results/{conversion-prompt,conversion-paths,results}.tsx + components/assess/assess-flow.tsx. TDD: rewrote the 2 persist-miss component tests (link -> button + onRetrySave + disabled-while-saving) + a new AssessFlow integration test (persist miss recovers to a real id, fetch called twice, wizard never re-run). Gate green: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, suite 1441 / 241 files. Branch mv-65-persist-miss-retry -> PR #15, founder-gated merge.

Fix: new pure lib/matches/sufficiency.ts#hasSufficientInputs (false ONLY when grade + English + budget are all absent; any one present ⇒ still render cards, never over-gate), checked upstream at the matches page (a matches-need-inputs prompt naming the missing inputs), lib/outcomes/freeze.ts (new 422 not-enough-data variant, no zeroed prediction persisted) and lib/plan/invalidate.ts (skip match-driven items). compute.ts + the MatchVerdict union are UNTOUCHED — a real `unknown` verdict band is deferred Layer B. Codex (GPT-5) adversarial review returned fix-then-ship; 4 findings all remediated TDD (auto-close falsely completing add-safer-options on abstain, vague gate copy, a bands-only over-gate premise, overstated comments) — its band-as-presence prescription was correctly rejected (it would reintroduce the fabrication). Gate: typecheck 0, lint 0, full suite green.

cards.title: Honest profile-completeness meter, not a fake accuracy score (audit C-6)
cards.summary: MV-124 Slice 8 (audit C-6). The old "profile accuracy" meter (lib/results/accuracy.ts) was dishonest three ways: completeness started at 25 and added only +3 for English taken (max 28) while the tiers required Verified>=40 / Complete>=75, so EVERY user was stranded at "Basic" (top tiers mathematically unreachable); the two document suggestions added zero points (dead items that never moved the bar); and it named a tier "Verified" + promised "band-level verification" though the app verifies nothing (nobody reads the uploaded PDF; the engine scores the typed numbers) — a false trust claim, the exact dishonesty the app exists to replace. Founder chose Option A: rebuild as an honest PROFILE COMPLETENESS meter (how much of the picture you've given us, never whether we checked it). New lib/results/completeness.ts#computeProfileCompleteness(profile, docs?): neutral reachable tiers Started(<50)/Detailed(50-99)/Full picture(=100); real weights — grade/English/budget x3 (the verdict-driving inputs the engine otherwise floors/assumes), field of study/target level/prior visa history x1 (denominator 12 on the anon surface, reaches exactly 100 when full); every suggestion raises the bar (no dead items); documents (transcript/financials x1) count ONLY when a docs presence signal is passed (signed-in vault), so they are never dead items on the anon results surface; dependents excluded (undefined = solo, no clean presence signal). New components/results/completeness-meter.tsx replaces accuracy-meter.tsx. The persisted payload key `accuracy` is deliberately kept (now typed ProfileCompleteness) so old stored rows don't crash. Second commit (Codex-reviewed): stale stored payloads — /assessment/[id] and the anon sessionStorage restore replay the stored payload, so pre-fix assessments still rendered the old "Verified" dishonesty; new normalizeStoredProfileCompleteness recomputes legacy/malformed meters from the persisted profile snapshot on read at BOTH sites, current payloads untouched (active users already refreshed by reScoreAssessment). Two separate dependents/financial-capacity bugs Codex surfaced are de-scoped to a follow-up chip. Gate green: typecheck 0, lint 0, goldens byte-identical, 2031 tests / 305 files. Commits 82ebda8 + 0b4a6a2. Dossier: cards/MV-144-honest-completeness-meter.md.
cards.badge: DONE — merged to master 2026-07-19 (PR #93, merge 2fc17ce). Codex second pass folded: stale stored payloads recompute honestly on read at both the owned DB page and the anon restore. Gate green (2031 tests).

cards.title: Dependents survive "not sure" and account bootstrap (financial-capacity honesty)
cards.summary: The two dependents/financial-capacity bugs Codex surfaced while reviewing MV-144 (chip task_9db5afb3), de-scoped from it to keep that slice the meter only. Both corrupt the DHA financial-capacity floor (lib/scoring/financial.ts prices declared dependents via auDependentsCapacityAud), so the verdict is wrong on money. Bug 1: lib/results/assemble.ts resolves destination "not-sure" -> "australia" BEFORE scoring (so the Australia DHA gate applies), but components/wizard/steps/budget-step.tsx gated the family/dependents control on destination === "australia" only — a not-sure student is scored against an Australia floor that silently assumes no dependents. Bug 2: lib/profiles/from-assessment.ts mapped every wizard answer EXCEPT dependents, so on claim / first signed-in assess a declared partner/children was dropped; the signed-in re-score reads dependents back from sections.family via lib/scoring/from-sections.ts#dependentsFromFamily, so the floor silently fell and an under-funded verdict could falsely soften. Fix: show the control for "australia" OR "not-sure"; map wizard dependents -> family section (spouse / spouse-and-kids), guarded so applying-alone omits the section (round-trips through dependentsFromFamily byte-for-byte, no dead alone write). Verified end-to-end: financial.ts genuinely reads dependents; ProfileSchema keeps dependents so profile_snapshot carries it; the mapping is the exact inverse of dependentsFromFamily. No scorer path touched (goldens byte-identical). Gate green: typecheck 0, lint 0, 2035 tests / 305 files (+4). Code commit 9d4aed7. Dossier: cards/MV-145-dependents-financial-capacity.md.
cards.badge: In Review — branch mv-145-dependents-financial-capacity (9d4aed7), founder-gated PR. Fixes two dependents/financial-capacity trust bugs de-scoped from MV-144: (1) the wizard family control is now shown for "not sure" (assessed as Australia), not only "australia", so the DHA floor isn't scored against an assumed-empty family; (2) declared dependents now survive account bootstrap (from-assessment.ts maps them onto the family section) instead of being dropped and silently lowering the floor on the signed-in re-score. TDD red->green (+4 tests), no scorer path touched (goldens byte-identical), gate green (2035 tests). Codex adversarial pass: CLEAN on both questions. No other surface gates dependents on destination (both match adapters price dependents ungated, profile family-editing/summaries are destination-independent, the proof-of-funds plan step is unconditional, and the signed-in re-score also resolves not-sure->AU); and the from-assessment guard round-trips every wizard-reachable state through dependentsFromFamily byte-for-byte. No fix required.

cards.title: Non-Google sign-in: email auth so students without a Google account can save/recover (audit F-6)
cards.summary: Audit F-6 (P0), flagged in the report as "Not on the board." Sign-in is Google-only (components/auth/auth-card.tsx:38-63 renders "Email sign-in isn't ready yet"); saving, converting, every (app) route, and the ONLY anonymous-recovery path all hard-require a Google account. A student without Google hits a wall at the exact conversion moment — a straight bounce for a consultancy-replacement product. Fix: add a non-Google email path via Supabase Auth (magic link / OTP recommended — password-free), wired into the SAME /auth/callback claim/bootstrap flow Google uses so save/convert/recover behave identically (do not fork the claim path). Supabase Auth sends its own OTP emails, so this does not hard-depend on the app-level transactional email infra F-7 flags absent — only production deliverability does. Founder nod on auth method; coordinate with the F-2 consent/age gate (MV-05). Distinct from F-7 (transactional email) and F-2/MV-05 (privacy/consent).

cards.title: Umbrella: Stage 1 tenancy foundation (MV-150 schema · MV-151 server boundary · MV-152 RLS · MV-153 negative-test gate)
cards.summary: READY (tracking) — umbrella for Stage 1 of the revised consultancy plan (tenancy foundation): organizations/memberships/cases/assignments/invitations/audit_events, the server-only case-permission boundary, case-aware RLS, and the real-Supabase cross-tenant test harness. Carries four slices — MV-150 (additive schema + deny-all RLS), MV-151 (getCaseContext/requireCasePermission + service-role exception list), MV-152 (SECURITY DEFINER RLS policies), MV-153 (negative catalogue + positive matrix harness) — in the DAG 150→{151,152}→153. Stage exit gate is MV-153: the authorization matrix passes positive AND negative real-DB tests under npm run test:integration; a green unit/lint run is NOT sufficient evidence. Not blocked by the Stage 0 legal gate (D-B): Stage 1 runs entirely on seed data, no real student data. Carries two still-open founder decisions as design inputs (deciding nothing): fate of an unclaimed case, and the bounded case-creation→student-notice window.

cards.title: Stage 1 tenancy core schema: six additive tables, deny-all RLS, regenerated types
cards.summary: Ships one additive migration creating the six Stage-1 tenancy tables (organizations, organization_memberships, cases, case_assignments, invitations, audit_events) per the plan's "New core tables", with the revision's invitation shape (unique token_hash, hash-only, nullable accepted_at/revoked_at/expires_at feeding the downstream single-acceptance CAS) and append-only audit (role-independent immutability trigger + SECURITY DEFINER writer choke point, bare-uuid tombstone columns). All six tables get enable+force RLS, explicit named deny-all policies, and revoke-all-from-client grants — real case-aware policies and grant review are MV-152's. Every FK and every column the Stage-1 RLS helpers will read is indexed (advisor-clean); text+check enums per house convention; lib/supabase/types.ts regenerated. Strictly additive: touches no existing table — the owner NOT NULL relaxation, program_predictions immutability-trigger backfill, predictions→attempts→outcomes composite-FK rebuild, document header/versions replacement, and storage.objects policy retirement from "Known schema obstacles" are all explicit Stage-2 non-goals.

cards.title: Case-permission server boundary (getCaseContext / requireCasePermission) + service-role exception list
cards.summary: Builds the server-only case-permission layer for the consultancy workspace: getCaseContext(actorUserId, caseId), requireCasePermission(actorUserId, caseId, permission), and the role→permission matrix (owner/admin = whole org, counsellor = assigned-only, student = linked-case-only, inactive membership = nothing, role read from the DB never from JWT/metadata). Establishes the enforcement-boundary doctrine — the authenticated client + RLS is the load-bearing tenant boundary and this layer is defense-in-depth — plus a machine-enforced service-role exception list (a registered allowlist + lint/test guard) so no new case-touching path can reach createSupabaseAdminClient unregistered. Unit + behavioral tests against a mocked client only; real-DB positive/negative proof is MV-153's exit gate. Depends on MV-150; consumed by MV-152 and MV-153.

cards.title: Case-aware RLS policies — replace deny-all with role-aware tenant isolation
cards.summary: Replaces MV-150's deny-all default policies with real case-aware RLS on all six tenancy tables (organizations, organization_memberships, cases, case_assignments, invitations, audit_events), routing every membership/assignment/case lookup through `private` SECURITY DEFINER STABLE helpers with pinned `search_path = ''` so policies stay non-recursive and plan on MV-150's indexes. Covers org owner/admin full-org access, counsellor assigned-only, student linked-case-only, and inactive-membership = no access; every UPDATE carries USING + WITH CHECK, grants are authenticated-only (anon gets nothing), and audit_events keeps its append-only shape. This is the load-bearing tenant-isolation layer per the plan's enforcement boundary — tested as the authenticated user, never service-role — with an EXPLAIN check proving index usage and once-per-statement helper evaluation, and a clean security+performance advisor pass. P1, agent-owned; blocked by MV-150, coordinates with MV-151's role matrix, consumed by MV-153's exit-gate harness.

cards.title: Cross-tenant negative-test harness + positive authorization matrix (Stage 1 exit gate)
cards.summary: The Stage 1 exit gate: a real-Supabase integration harness that proves the tenancy authorization matrix both DENIES and GRANTS. Extends the *.itest.ts pattern + localhost hard-guard from tests/integration/anon-purge.itest.ts, but adds the capability the two existing itests lack — per-role AUTHENTICATED clients (anon key + user JWT), because RLS only proves anything when queries run as the actual user; the service-role admin bypasses RLS and is used only for seeding/teardown and for exercising MV-151's service-role exception wrappers. A two-org fixture factory mints 2 orgs x users in every role (owner/admin/counsellor/student) x cases + assignments + student links. Implements the Stage-1 slice of the plan's negative catalogue (cross-org list/read/change/delete deny across all six tenant tables; unassigned-counsellor deny; student cross-case deny; revoked-member immediate loss; role forgery from user/app-metadata rejected; service-role path rejects unauthorized case ids) AND the positive matrix in the same run (an all-deny bug passes every negative test while breaking the product). Wires the CI integration job to export the new anon key and keeps the 0-skipped/>0-passed guard so the suite can never green having tested nothing. Depends on MV-150+151+152. Stage 1 cannot exit until this suite is green as a gating check.

cards.title: Umbrella: Stage 2 case-aware core (MV-155 personal cases + backfill · MV-156 owner-nullable + composite-FK rebase · MV-157 case-aware data access · MV-158 anonymous claim · MV-159 RLS · MV-160 tighten + stage exit)
cards.summary: Umbrella (tracking) for Stage 2 of the revised consultancy plan (case-aware core): additive-migration-sequence steps 2–13, moving the nine student-owned tables (profiles, assessments, plan_items, user_program_state, documents, document_status, program_predictions, application_attempts, outcome_events) off owner-keyed onto case-keyed, and moving the server layer off "actor equals student" onto MV-151's getCaseContext/requireCasePermission. Six slices — MV-155 (personal case per existing owner at migration + nullable case_id + backfill, incl. the program_predictions immutability-trigger obstacle), MV-156 (owner NOT NULL relax on the eight tables + predictions→attempts→outcomes composite-FK rebase onto unique(id, case_id)), MV-157 (repositories/routes onto case authorization + dual-write), MV-158 (the anonymous claim — the plan's "hardest dual-write site"), MV-159 (case-aware RLS on the migrated tables, extending MV-152's SECURITY DEFINER pattern), MV-160 (case_id NOT NULL, drop the compensating checks, prove the exit) — in the DAG 155→156→[157+158, ONE PR]→159→160. MV-157 and MV-158 ship as a single pull request (one branch, separate commits): master IS production and Vercel auto-deploys from it, so "merge but do not deploy" was never executable and merging MV-157 alone opens the owner-set/case_id-null claim window both cards forbid; the combined merge is additionally gated on MV-155's and MV-156's migrations being APPLIED AND RECONCILED on the hosted database, not merely merged. Stage exit gate, verbatim from the plan: "existing students see the same correct data, while case-scoped repositories no longer depend on actor equals student" — proven by MV-160 as STUDENT-VISIBLE PAYLOAD equivalence per user × per domain plus row-identity parity (NOT byte-identical rows, which MV-155's new column, the set_updated_at trigger and MV-156's surrogate keys all make impossible), split into a synthetic CI suite that never skips and a rehearsal-only live replay the integrator runs against a copy. Stage 2 expands NO grant: write is proved on five tables, read on nine, and INSERT on profiles/assessments/plan_items/documents is deferred to Stage 3 with its grant list in specs/2026-08-02-stage2-migration-and-access-matrix.md §6, pinned by a 42501 negative. Service-role retreat is measured as disposition, not as zero: each of the ten legacy-owner-scoped entries is either retired or re-justified with a named later stage. This is the FIRST stage that mutates LIVE user data, so the reversibility doctrine binds every slice: a rehearsal on a copy of live data and a stated rollback with its named point of no return, recorded before any production run. Not blocked by the still-open pilot-consultancy item (Stage 0 exit); IS the hard prerequisite for Stage 3, because a consultancy case has no Auth user and no row can exist for one while owner stays NOT NULL.

cards.title: Stage 2 personal cases + `case_id` columns + owner→case backfill across nine student-owned tables
cards.summary: Stage 2 steps 2-7, and the first card in the whole programme that mutates LIVE user data. Creates one personal case per existing Auth user AT MIGRATION (not first-use), adds a NULLABLE `case_id` to all nine student-owned tables (profiles, assessments, plan_items, user_program_state, documents, document_status, program_predictions, application_attempts, outcome_events), backfills it from the current `owner` relationship, and ships ALL the per-case uniqueness indexes — FULL, not partial on `case_id is not null`, because PostgREST's bare `on_conflict=` cannot infer a partial index and every MV-157 upsert against one would raise 42P10 (NULLs are distinct in a unique index, so the nullable window is safe without the predicate) — alongside the surviving per-owner ones (MV-157 creates none of them and ships no migration; MV-160 drops the legacy ones). Carries the plan's `program_predictions` immutability obstacle as a first-class criterion: `private.reject_prediction_update()` is narrowed to permit exactly a `case_id` null→not-null transition with every other column byte-identical, and MV-160 restores the unconditional body as its last statement. Rewrites the six flat table-level write grants into explicit column lists, with a deliberate ASYMMETRY that is the point of the section: `case_id` is OUT of every UPDATE list (re-pointing a row into another case is the hazard) and IN the five INSERT lists on user_program_state, document_status, program_predictions, application_attempts and outcome_events — without which MV-157's dual-write hits 42501 with no card owning the gap. The two PostgREST UPSERT paths are closed by a SECURITY DEFINER trigger deriving `case_id` from `owner`, so no UPDATE(case_id) grant is needed — qualified `when (new.owner is not null)`, so a consultancy row (owner NULL) keeps the case_id it supplies and is bounded by MV-159's WITH CHECK instead; unqualified, the trigger had nothing to derive from and its overwrite hardening made MV-160's counsellor-write proof unsatisfiable. All three new `private` definer objects carry `revoke all on function … from public` in the same migration, per the Stage 1 discipline — `authenticated` already holds USAGE on `private`. Anonymous (owner-null) assessments stay deliberately case-less and keep purging under MV-135's 3-day policy; the documents header/versions REPLACEMENT, `storage.objects` re-scoping, owner-nullable relaxation, composite-FK rebase, repository migration and case-aware RLS are all explicit non-goals (Stage 4 / MV-156 / MV-157 / MV-159). Ships with a rehearsal on a restored copy of live data and an ordered rollback that expires when MV-157 merges — and is superseded by the stage-level reverse sweep the moment MV-156 applies.

cards.title: Owner nullable on the eight NOT NULL tables + predictions→attempts→outcome_events composite-FK rebase onto the case
cards.summary: Step 8 of the plan's additive sequence plus two of the six known schema obstacles, in one transactional migration: relax `owner` to nullable on all eight NOT NULL student-owned tables (profiles, plan_items, user_program_state, documents, document_status, program_predictions, application_attempts, outcome_events — `assessments.owner` is already nullable and is not one of them), and re-base the predictions→attempts→outcome_events ownership chain from `unique (id, owner)` composite-FK targets onto `unique (id, case_id)` with re-pointed child keys and covering indexes. This is the hard prerequisite for Stage 3 — a consultancy case has no Auth user, so no row can exist for one while the constraint stands — and it carries two traps the plan's prose does not: `user_program_state` and `document_status` key `owner` in their PRIMARY KEY, so a PK column cannot simply drop NOT NULL (each needs a surrogate `id` PK plus a FULL unique on the legacy pair — `user_program_state_owner_program_idx (owner, program_id)` and `document_status_owner_kind_idx (owner, kind)` — and MV-160 must drop those two as well. CORRECTED 2026-08-03 from `partial unique … where owner is not null`: PostgREST's bare `on_conflict=` emits a plain column list and cannot infer a PARTIAL index, so `setObtained` and `upsertProgramState` — both live today — would raise 42P10 on real requests for the whole MV-156→MV-157 window; the predicate bought nothing because NULLs are distinct in a unique index. Nothing is re-keyed onto `case_id`: a PK column cannot be null and `case_id` stays nullable until MV-160, so the surrogate was the only available shape), and Postgres FKs default to MATCH SIMPLE, so a composite key containing a nullable `case_id` is silently unenforced for null rows — the divergence-is-structurally-impossible invariant the chain was built for is absent precisely during the half-migrated window. Mitigated by a validated `check (owner is not null or case_id is not null)` named `<table>_ownership_axis_present` on ALL EIGHT tables — explicitly NOT `check (case_id is not null)`, which was drafted and rejected because a CHECK is role-independent, service_role does not bypass it, and every live outcomes insert today writes owner and no case_id, so that shape takes the production write path down with 23514 for the whole MV-156→MV-157 window; the accepted consequence is that MV-160's SET NOT NULL gets NO scan-free flip and takes a full scan (negligible at 39 rows). MV-160 drops all eight checks, none survives into Stage 3. Also mitigated by retaining the legacy owner chain alongside the new case chain until MV-160, by ordering `drop not null` last inside one transaction, and by an itest that demonstrates the MATCH SIMPLE hole with the check dropped so nobody removes it without knowing what it buys. Mutates live schema on real user data, so MV-154's rehearsal-on-a-copy and stated rollback apply — the rollback must also DROP the two surrogate `id` columns (restoring the composite PKs alone leaves a third schema shape, not the original), and it is clean only while zero NULL-owner rows exist.

cards.title: Case-aware data access: repositories and routes move off actor-equals-student onto case authorization + `case_id` (dual-write)
cards.summary: Steps 9-10 of the plan's additive migration sequence, and the half of the Stage 2 exit gate that says "case-scoped repositories no longer depend on actor equals student". Moves the student-data repositories (profiles, assessments-read, plan, matches/user_program_state, documents, document_status, outcomes orchestrators) and the 15 routes / 11 Server Components above them off the `.eq("owner", userId)` predicate onto a resolved `case_id` + MV-151's `requireCasePermission`, with one writer helper enforcing the dual-write rule (case_id ALWAYS; owner only where the case has a student_user_id, derived from `cases.student_user_id` and never caller-supplied, so the two can never disagree). Ships NO migration: the case-keyed uniqueness indexes are MV-155 §E's — two cards creating the same indexes means one apply fails or is a silent no-op — so what remains here is the application half, moving every PostgREST `onConflict` target onto MV-155's case-scoped indexes and proving each with a real-DB upsert-twice test. Introduces `lib/cases/personal-case.ts` with `ensurePersonalCase(sessionUser, db?)` taking the VERIFIED Supabase User object and deriving display_name/email internally, so no client-supplied identity string can reach `cases`. Also rewrites every `legacy-owner-scoped` entry in MV-151's service-role exception registry: paths whose grants already allow it (shortlist) flip to the authenticated client and leave the list; the rest keep an entry whose `requiredCaseCheck` now names a real case check, with the flip deferred to Stage 3's grant review or Stage 4 Storage. HARD-BLOCKED BY MV-156 (Done before this card starts — it moves the primary keys this card writes repository code against), and SHIPS IN ONE PULL REQUEST WITH MV-158: master is production and Vercel auto-deploys, so merging this card alone creates the owner-set/case_id-null claim window; the combined merge is gated on MV-155's and MV-156's migrations being applied and reconciled on the hosted database. Preserves the personal student experience byte-for-byte (per-repo and per-route equivalence snapshots); the production-shaped before/after regression and the stage exit are MV-160's. Owner NULLABLE + composite-FK rebase (MV-156), case-aware RLS on these tables (MV-159), and the document header/versions replacement (Stage 4) are explicit non-goals.

cards.title: Anonymous claim under the case model: create-or-resolve a personal case, dual-write owner + case_id atomically, every MV-130 / MV-135 leg preserved
cards.summary: The plan's named "hardest dual-write site" (Known schema obstacles, line 329), carved as its own card because it is the one write path where a partial failure silently destroys a converting student's work — and shipped in ONE PULL REQUEST with MV-157, because master is production and Vercel auto-deploys from it, so merging MV-157 alone opens exactly the window this card closes. Moves the anonymous-assessment claim onto the case model across all four entry points — Google OAuth, the MV-147 emailed 6-digit code, the emailed link, and the signed-in recover-in-place POST /api/assess/claim — so a claim create-or-resolves the claimer's personal case (idempotent, before any write, through MV-157's `ensurePersonalCase(sessionUser)`, which takes the verified Auth User and derives display_name/email internally rather than accepting caller-supplied strings it could never prove came from a session), then binds owner + case_id + claimed_at in ONE conditional statement, because two sequential updates leave an owned-but-case-less row that case-scoped repositories cannot see and the student's assessment vanishes from their own dashboard. Preserves the shipped interactions exactly rather than re-deriving them: MV-130's five honest recovery reasons (already-mine / claimed / expired / error, plus a NEW retryable leg when personal-case resolution fails, which must never render as a false "expired"), MV-135's purge contract (owner is null stays the load-bearing predicate — a claimed-but-case-less row must survive, and anonymous rows stay case-less so the purge index still matches), and the assessments_primary_idx partial unique, which during the dual-key window must be satisfied under BOTH the legacy (owner) and the new (case_id) predicates or the promote fails and the dashboard re-pins to the first assessment ever claimed — the exact MV-16 regression. Also asserts the invariant MV-160's tighten relies on: every successful claim leg leaves owner non-null whenever claimed_at is set. Requires real-DB integration tests (extends tests/integration/claim-path.itest.ts) because a supabase-js mock cannot reject a write a partial unique index rejects; the gate is typecheck · lint · test · test:integration, all four now GATING under the no-bypass master ruleset, run on the combined branch.

cards.title: Case-aware RLS for the migrated student-owned tables (Stage 2 step 11)
cards.summary: Extends MV-152's RLS discipline from the six tenancy tables to the nine migrated student-owned tables (profiles, assessments, plan_items, user_program_state, documents, document_status, program_predictions, application_attempts, outcome_events), so the database — not just MV-157's repositories — enforces case scoping: `private` SECURITY DEFINER STABLE helpers with pinned empty `search_path` (including a new uncorrelated `actor_case_ids()` for the measured InitPlan shape), USING + WITH CHECK on every mutating policy, `case_id`/`owner` kept out of the column-level UPDATE grant so re-pointing a row into another case is unexpressible, and a grant set unchanged from the POST-MV-155 baseline — captured column-granularly from the migrated stack, never transcribed from a dossier, because MV-155 §H already replaced six flat verbs with column lists and put case_id into the five INSERT lists. This card re-scopes rows; it hands `authenticated` no verb it lacked. That refusal was tested and UPHELD by the integrator against MV-160's original exit criterion, which required counsellor INSERTs on profiles/assessments/plan_items/documents — verbs `authenticated` simply does not hold, so no policy here could have granted them; those four move to Stage 3 with their exact grant list in specs/2026-08-02-stage2-migration-and-access-matrix.md §6, pinned by a 42501 negative in MV-160's suite. Replaces the three `pp/aa/oe` INSERT policies' inline `exists` subqueries (an anti-recursion violation and a silent-denial hazard once peer tables gain policies) with case-parentage helpers, ships the transitional `owner OR case_id` disjunct that keeps not-yet-backfilled rows visible to their real owners until MV-160 drops it, keeps anonymous assessments invisible to every authenticated client, preserves the program_predictions immutability trigger and outcome_events append-only shape, and adds the `to authenticated` clause `documents`' two legacy policies never had (they apply to PUBLIC including anon, and only the absent grant keeps anon out — note they are ALREADY in the `(select auth.uid())` InitPlan form since 20260618120000, so there is no bare-auth.uid() defect to find). cards.title: Stage 3 slice 5 — render the existing experience inside an explicit case route
cards.summary: Plan bullet 3, and the largest surface in the stage. Renders the existing MeroVisa experience (profile, matches, plan, documents, checklist) under an explicit case route for a case that is NOT the actor's own — the first time a non-student actor reaches student data through the product. Flips app/api/plan/action/route.ts off service-role onto the authenticated client (retiring registry entry 8) and SPLITS app/api/profile/section/route.ts — its profile write moves, but reScoreAssessment (assessments UPDATE result), invalidatePlan's generator-column copy refresh (impact/title/body/estimates) and adoptOwnerKeyedResidue (UPDATE case_id) are all refused by spec §6.1 and stay service-role, so entry 9 NARROWS rather than retires; all three would fail SILENTLY if flipped (re-score.ts:33 never destructures error, and throwOnError appears nowhere in lib/ or app/). Those moves ARE grants 1 and 5, which is why MV-168 is a hard predecessor (without it this slice ships the case route still on service-role, the exact inverse of the enforcement boundary). Depends on MV-171 for a real student-less case to exercise: before it, the route can only be tested against a personal case, which is the Stage 2 shape and proves nothing new. NOT IN SCOPE: any change to the documents model, Storage paths, or signed downloads (Stage 4 — object paths stay owner-keyed through Stage 3 by the Stage 2 spec §8 decision); the case-context indicators (MV-173). PLUS F-8, which said FIVE and is SEVEN (spec amended in PR #143): shortlist:46, documents/status:33, outcomes/prediction:28, outcomes/attempt:31, outcomes/event:32, AND plan/action:37 + profile/section:37 — the last two were missed because they were VISIBLE to the service-role registry lens, which gave them a client disposition and asked nothing about their case id. All seven resolve the ACTOR'S OWN personal case via resolvePersonalCaseId and accept no case id — left as-is, every write control in the case route writes to the COUNSELLOR'S own case, and nothing fails loudly because the grants and policies already exist. They take an explicit, authorized case id here. Access matrix cells 13-17 and 21-23 in spec §4; exit criterion E7.

cards.title: Stage 3 slice 6 — case-context indicators, and closing the student field-allowlist gap (F-3)
cards.summary: Plan bullet 4, plus the trust bug the list surface exposes. Persistent, unmissable indication of WHOSE case the actor is in and whether it is their own — a counsellor editing a student's profile must never be able to mistake it for their own data. PLUS the TYPESCRIPT field allowlist that lib/cases/permissions.ts and lib/cases/README.md both record ('a Stage 3 mutation that accepts an arbitrary case patch from a student is a defect even though this cell allows the claim'); README.md:152-157 locates the remedy — 'the allowlist belongs with that mutation'. NOT IN SCOPE: F-3's column guard. cases grants authenticated UPDATE on (archived_at, display_name, email, operational_status) and enforce_case_write_surface guards only archived_at and operational_status, so display_name and email ARE student-writable and MV-170's list renders exactly those two to a counsellor — but that omission is the CANONICAL decision, not a gap (stage1-canonical-access-matrix.md:68-70 'the student's write surface is profile fields only'; 20260730180000_case_aware_rls_policies.sql:459 'display_name, email — profile fields. The student's surface'), and it is pinned POSITIVELY by tests/integration/case-rls.itest.ts:833. Narrowing it turns that Stage 1 test red, which spec §5 defines as proof a slice moved a canonical cell and is wrong. F-3 is escalated to the FOUNDER alongside F-1; the impersonation risk is real, and under reading (a) it is mitigated at MV-170's display layer, not the write layer. NOT IN SCOPE: consultancy-internal notes (F-4 — the case.notes.internal permission exists but no column or table does; Stage 4 owns case activity, and no slice invents a notes model to satisfy a permission constant).

cards.title: Stage 3 slice 7 — service-role retreat and the stage exit gate
cards.summary: CARRIES THE STAGE EXIT. Completes the service-role disposition (spec §6.2): reclassify entries 1 and 2 to 'sanctioned' (F-6 — app/(focused)/assessment/[id]/page.tsx serves an UNAUTHENTICATED visitor so no grant to authenticated can ever retire it, and app/api/account/delete/route.ts says 'DELIBERATELY still owner-keyed' in its own justification; both are permanent designs mislabelled as grandfathered, so the list currently reports two entries as awaiting a migration that will never come), narrow entries 3, 4 AND 9 (app/api/profile/section/route.ts does NOT retire — reScoreAssessment, the plan copy refresh and adoptOwnerKeyedResidue are all refused by spec §6.1, and service-role-exceptions.test.ts:280/:293 pin both horns, so a builder cannot keep the admin client and delete the entry), confirm 5-7 wait for Stage 4's Storage policies, and register the new case-scoped scoring route. Net 9 → 9 — the same count it started with, one retired and one added — and the growth is admitted rather than hidden: MV-154's framing of the list as monotonically shrinking does not survive Stage 3, and the stage is scored on scope, not on list size. THEN proves the exit gate — seven criteria E1-E7 at named layers (spec §9.1), each shipping the vacuity guard from §9.2. E4 is the direct analogue of the Stage 2 §A2 vacuity MV-165 recorded honestly: it passes trivially if the case under test has a student_user_id, or on an empty write set, so it must assert cases.student_user_id IS NULL, owner IS NULL on every row written, AND a created-row count > 0. E1 must assert the actor's JWT role is 'authenticated' (a test run as service_role bypasses every policy and proves nothing). E6 must assert per-entry disposition, never a count (the tracked set is 9 at exit). E7 pins F-8: each case-scoped write route must write the STUDENT'S case id, read back from the row — and the counsellor fixture must itself hold a personal case with a row on the same table, or a wrong-case write has nowhere to land and the test proves nothing. AND THE EXIT MUST NOT OVERCLAIM (spec §9.3): with D-B shut, production holds no consultancy org and no student-less case, so a green Stage 3 licenses 'the mechanism is built and proven under RLS as the authenticated user' and NEVER 'it works for real students' — that is earned in Stage 7's pilot.

cards.title: A repeated query parameter 500s the sign-in page
cards.summary: Confirmed defect on a page LIVE IN PRODUCTION, found while reviewing MV-170 (PR #136) but outside that slice. Next hands a repeated query parameter through as string[] (its own SearchParams type is {[key:string]: string | string[] | undefined}), but app/(marketing)/auth/page.tsx declared searchParams as {next?: string; assessment?: string} — a claim about the URL, not about Next, and one TypeScript cannot check across a framework boundary. So /auth?next=/a&next=/b reached safeNext, which calls input.startsWith, and 500d the sign-in page; ?next= alone did the same because [] is truthy; the array also flowed into AuthCards nextPath prop typed string; and a repeated ?assessment= silently signed NO claim (String([a,b]) is "a,b", which fails the id shape check), costing a visitor from anonymous results the assessment the token binds. A CRASH, NOT A SECURITY HOLE — safeNext returning null is already the safe path and the throw precedes the redirect, so no unsafe destination was ever followed; the redirect-safety logic is correct and is NOT restructured. Fix matches MV-170s own approach: widen both declared types to the truthful union and collapse to the first value at the boundary, via ONE shared lib/http/search-params.ts first() rather than a third private copy; an empty array reads as ABSENT, not "". app/(focused)/assess/page.tsx never called a string method on a search param so it never threw — a repeated ?new=/?error= was silently IGNORED instead; it now honours the first value, which is the one behaviour delta in the card and is flagged for the founder rather than buried. MV-170s private first() is behaviourally identical and lives on OPEN PR #136, not on master, so it is deliberately not in this diff: whichever of the two PRs merges second swaps it for the import (one-line, same behaviour). Red test came first and failed with the production error verbatim — TypeError: input.startsWith is not a function; six mutations (helper x3, /auth x2, /assess x1) each re-run RED. Gate green unpiped: typecheck 0, lint 0, test 0 (342 files, 2769 tests, +21), build 0.

cards.title: The redirect origin is taken from a request header on trust
cards.summary: lib/auth/site-origin.ts falls back to the x-forwarded-host / host request header when NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is unset, and that value becomes the ORIGIN half of ${origin}${destination} at app/auth/callback/route.ts:36 — independently of safeNext, which only validates the destination half. Surfaced by the adversarial pass over safe-next.ts during PR #137 (MV-176) review and, separately, by the 2026-07-10 audit. NOT a safeNext bypass and not live on Vercel: measured 2026-08-11 that a forged x-forwarded-host does not move the production Location (the edge overwrites it) and that a forged Host 404s. The fallback is NOT dead — NODE_ENV=development already handles local dev, so the branch serves Vercel PREVIEWS, whose per-PR URLs no fixed NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL can express. Fail-closed was rejected (turns a latent security risk into a live sign-in outage, and breaks previews); leave-it-documented was rejected (.env.example still omits the var, so a fresh deploy starts in the untrusted branch). CHOSEN: bound the trust without removing the branch — consult the header only when the runtime is Vercel, the one edge whose overwrite is measured, and validate the result in MV-176 round-trip idiom (parse it; accept only an exact origin — http(s), no credentials, no path/query/fragment). PLUS a second defect found in the same branch: a comma-joined x-forwarded-host from a proxy CHAIN makes NextResponse.redirect throw, 500ing the sign-in page — the same failure class MV-176 just fixed, reached through a header. Every new rejection degrades to url.origin, so no new path can 500 and none can emit an uncertified origin.

cards.title: Document collaboration schema: versions and reviews (Stage 4 slice 2)
cards.summary: case_document_versions + case_document_reviews as additive tables BESIDE the vault, with RLS, column-scoped grants and MV-182's two forbidden-grant assertions. documents keeps UNIQUE (case_id, kind) — dropping the arbiter index would break every .upsert() on documents at plan time, so the plan's "replacing the one-per-kind model" is superseded by the spec. cards.badge: Done — merged to master 2026-08-21 (PR #152, merge b57af21) and applied to production. Two additive tables beside the vault (RLS enabled+forced, column-scoped grants, no UPDATE grant at all, eleven apply-time assertions). cards.title: Case-scoped Storage and signed downloads (Stage 4 slice 3)
cards.summary: The second half of the 5B split, sequenced after MV-185 and before MV-186 (the number is higher only because the plan reserved MV-186-189). Adds the case/<case_id>/<version_id> prefix and its storage.objects policy, a short-TTL signed-download helper authorized BEFORE the URL is minted, and makes the three document routes accept a NAMED case id. Corrects the plan: the routes are already case-scoped (MV-157 §G) — the real gap is that all three resolve the ACTOR'S OWN case, which is F-8. Existing owner-keyed vault objects are deliberately not migrated.
cards.badge: Done — merged to master 2026-08-21 (PR #153, merge 8ab5d92) and applied to production. Spec §6 overturned BOTH of the card's data premises before a line was written. (A) NO storage.objects policy — the bucket already denies `case/` to every client (foldername[1] is the literal `case`, no uid) and all writes are service_role, so a SELECT policy would be a second and weaker path to bytes only an authorized mint reaches; defended by a denial test WITH A CONTROL, an ADDITIVE mutant that plants the declined policy, and an apply-time guard. (B) `id` joins the versions INSERT grant — decided by write ORDERING, since without it a failed upload strands a version row with no DELETE grant to retract it — plus the CHECK on storage_path, a table constraint so it binds service_role too. 6 mutants each killed distinct NAMED tests (20 collected, 0 worker crashes); 11 apply-time guards and 5 code guards each falsified. MV-186 is the writer it deliberately stopped short of.

cards.title: Document collaboration UI: upload, version history, review verbs (Stage 4 slice 4, PR 5C)
cards.summary: Closes the Stage 4 loop: MV-182 could ask for a document, MV-185 gave a file a row, MV-190 gave it a path — nothing could still RECEIVE or JUDGE one. Ships the pure five-state derivation, two write routes (a version against a request; a review on a version), one read route (a signed download per version), and the Documents page UI. Carries the spec §7 pass: case_document_requests.status is LOSSY — three human states collapse into `outstanding` (nothing arrived / awaiting OUR review / rejected) and two into `resolved` (accepted, or marked received by hand), so a page built on the column alone points the chase at the wrong person. Status is never written by this slice; the after-insert triggers write it and a guard trigger refuses a contradicting hand-written value. NO MIGRATION — the schema is already live in production. Both tables stay append-only: no delete-a-version and no edit-a-review control. Also corrects MV-183's lodgement scope note, which claimed "nothing here has been checked or approved" — now false in one direction, and corrected without letting the panel claim it can tell an accepted file from one received by hand.
cards.badge: Done — merged to master 2026-08-21 (PR #154, merge 15e87c1). Closed the Stage 4 loop: the five-state derivation (D6), two write routes, one read route (D9), and the Documents page. D10 kept document_id NULL so the vault's UNIQUE (case_id, kind) could not silently replace a student's file. 25 mutants each killed distinct NAMED tests; ONE KILLED NOTHING and found two fixture bugs (an all-digit uuid made .toUpperCase() a no-op; a 10-byte PDF never reached verifyFileMagic's 12-byte floor) — both now in MISTAKES.md. NO MIGRATION, so one PR.

cards.title: Document access audit events (Stage 4 slice 5)
cards.summary: Pays the part of the service-role debt Stage 4 owns. The plan makes auditing a CONDITION of the exception list — every entry 'named, justified, preceded by an explicit case authorization check, and audited' — and lib/supabase/service-role-exceptions.ts holds 18 sanctioned entries with all 18 carrying auditEvent: null, so the fourth clause is satisfied by none of them. Today a counsellor can upload, open and download a student's passport scan and nothing anywhere records that it happened. Wires the five document-access paths (two uploads, two signed-URL mints, one delete) to public.audit_events through a single choke point. Spec §8 (D11-D15) first, committed before code.
cards.badge: Done — merged to master 2026-08-22 (PR #155, merge 20757a1). No migration: `service_role` already held INSERT on `public.audit_events`, live and empty since Stage 1. D11 was PROVEN rather than argued — EXECUTE was granted to both `service_role` and `authenticated`, the schema cache reloaded, and PostgREST still answered 404 PGRST202 ("searched for the function public.write_audit_event"); forcing Content-Profile: private answered 406 PGRST106 naming the two exposed schemas. No grant fixes schema exposure, so `private.write_audit_event` stays inert by design and the write is a direct INSERT. D12 fail-closed on the plan's "cannot be separated" (line 504): the two signed-URL mints audit BEFORE minting, the three mutations after their effect commits, and no route returns 2xx without its audit row. D13 is a CLOSED metadata allow-list, not a deny-list, because `original_name` is a user-supplied filename and in this corridor carries the student's own name. D15 threads the case's real organization through `resolveTargetCase` with no extra round trip — `NULL = ANY(...)` is NULL, so a null-org row is readable by nobody, ever. 14 mutants, 14 killed. Scope fenced by test: the other thirteen exception entries must stay null. Production verified unchanged after the PostgREST probe — function ACL back to owner-only, audit_events still 0 rows.

cards.title: Stage 4 exit gate: prove the document boundary holds (Stage 4 slice 6)
cards.summary: The verification half of Stage 4's exit gate: "an unauthorized actor cannot upload, view, download, review, or enumerate a document, and the authorized request-to-approval flow works." Five negative verbs and one positive walk. Starts with a COVERAGE INVENTORY rather than a test, because Stage 4 already has a lot of green that does not add up to the gate: the collaboration walk itest proves only the happy path and only for an authorized actor; tests/api/case-denial.test.ts is route-level and mocked, so it proves the route refuses and not that the database would have; MV-153's real-Supabase matrix carries the case/org permission verbs but not the document ones; and `enumerate` appears to be covered by nothing at all. Extends tenant-isolation.itest.ts rather than starting a new harness. No migration expected — if a real hole needs a schema change, stop and report rather than folding a migration into a verification slice.
cards.badge: Done — merged to master 2026-08-23 (PR #157, merge c1e3022). No migration, so nothing was owed to the production ledger. Gate taken: the coverage inventory found FOUR real gaps (enumerate uncovered in all four sub-modes; anon probed for read but never write; the mint denial mock-only; existence parity unasserted) and closed them in tests/integration/stage4-exit-gate.itest.ts (50 tests). 28 mutant-test pairs across 8 widening mutants, hitting 25 DISTINCT tests — a denial dies to permissiveness, not to a drop, so MV-185-style drop mutants would have left every denial green. THE RESULT WORTH KEEPING: the download boundary is defended independently in RLS AND TypeScript — each survives the other being widened, and only the compound mutant kills the mint denials. Three mutants survived deliberately and are recorded as findings. Also struck a deferral MV-190 had silently discharged (DEFERRED_BY_DESIGN 7 -> 6). CI green on all four checks; integration self-hosts its stack and reported Test Files 20 passed (20) / Tests 1014 passed (1014) in 90.4s of real test time — read from the RAW LOG, not the summary, because a crashed worker prints a clean summary having run nothing. PRE-MERGE REVIEW: a 29-agent adversarial pass raised 23 findings, 20 refuted and 3 survived. All three were in the mutation EVIDENCE rather than in the tests or the product, and all three were fixed in 62eeb99 before merge: (1) stale prose contradicting the file's own results table; (2) a kill total that reconciled with neither the row sum 28 nor the distinct union 25, because versions_select_org's three kills are a strict subset of versions_select_true's nine; (3) the anonymous storage-WRITE assertion kills no mutant, since both storage mutants plant `for select` policies only and one is scoped `to authenticated` — now disclosed as a residual limit naming the missing `anon_storage_write` addition mutant, with the property still guarded by 20260821150000's fail-closed check on polqual OR polwithcheck. RESIDUE FOR THE NEXT READER: the coverage inventory's positive-walk row cites stage4-collaboration-walk.itest.ts, which runs entirely on the service-role client — two independent reviewers read that as the positive walk being UNPROVEN and both were wrong (it IS proven under RLS end to end at stage4-document-collaboration.itest.ts:945 via an authenticated actor's client), but the citation invites the misreading and should be repointed. SCOPE: verification only — Stage 4's scanning/quarantine/backup bullet is pilot-gated and excluded, and Stage 3's own exit gate (MV-174) is still Backlog with no dossier, so "Stage 4 passed" must not be read as "Stages 1-4 all passed".

cards.title: A shebanged scripts/*.mjs breaks its importing test file on Windows
cards.summary: tests/integration/stage2-data-equivalence.itest.ts fails to PARSE on Windows with `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token`, because its line 79 imports `scripts/stage2/capture-read-path-snapshot.mjs`, which opens with `#!/usr/bin/env node`. Vitest's SSR transform hoists CJS interop shims above the `#!`, and a shebang is only legal at byte 0. This is the rule already in MISTAKES.md. The fix is the one that entry prescribes: move the importable logic (READ_PATHS through formatDiff — one serializer, one hash, one exclusion list) into a shebang-free sibling `scripts/stage2/read-path-snapshot.mjs` that BOTH the CLI entrypoint and the test import, leaving the shebang on the thin CLI wrapper. Ships with a platform-independent regression guard: scan every tests/** import of scripts/**/*.mjs and refuse a `#!` first byte.
cards.badge: Done — merged to master 2026-08-23 (PR #158, merge bb4c01b). No migration. A CRLF-terminated `#!` is the trigger, NOT the shebang alone: a three-way probe on one Windows host measured CRLF-terminated `#!` -> SyntaxError, the SAME `#!` with an LF ending -> parses, no `#!` -> parses. So it is neither jsdom-only (this failure was in the `node` lane) nor about node-builtin imports, and it is Windows-only for a mechanical reason — a CRLF checkout breaks, Linux CI's LF checkout does not. THE EXPENSIVE CONSEQUENCE: a file that fails to PARSE collects ZERO tests, so an importing suite can be silently dead locally while CI ticks every one of its tests. stage2-data-equivalence.itest.ts was dead on Windows across five cards' worth of "pre-existing, not mine" notes (MV-165/168/185/186/190) before anyone chased it. FIX: the importable logic moved wholesale into shebang-free `scripts/stage2/read-path-snapshot.mjs`, `#!` left on the thin CLI wrapper, byte-identical on both halves (11,548 B shared + 5,470 B CLI) — which is what protects MV-160 §A's one-serializer-one-hash-one-exclusion-list guarantee. GUARD: tests/scripts/mjs-imports-are-shebang-free.test.ts reads BYTES off disk, so it bites on LF and CRLF alike rather than only where the parse happens to break; it ran 3 tests in CI's validate job. MISTAKES.md was wrong twice over and is rewritten around the measurement. NOTE FOR A COLD READER: the badge's local result of `Test Files 19 passed (19)` / `Tests 964 passed (964)` was measured BEFORE MV-191 merged; locally it is now 20/1014. It is a dated measurement, not a claim about today. CI on the merged head: integration 20 files / 1014 tests / 109.4s of real test time, validate 387 files / 3889 tests — read from the RAW LOG, because a crashed worker prints a clean summary having run nothing.

cards.title: Stage 5 slice 1 — mint and revoke a student invitation (the bridge's write half)
cards.summary: The first slice of Stage 5, the bridge between the two versions of the product: a counsellor mints a single-use, hash-only invitation for a case and can revoke it. Four facts were measured before carving and remove work a reader would assume. (1) The `invitations` table is COMPLETE — MV-150 shipped it and `invitations_shape_check` already makes a malformed invitation unrepresentable, so NO MIGRATION. (2) The grant set is deliberately narrow and IS the design: `authenticated` holds select+insert and `update (revoked_at)` only — `accepted_at` is not grantable, which is what keeps acceptance server-only for slice 2; widening it to pass a test is the failure mode to refuse. (3) Email OTP sign-in already exists, so Stage 5's first bullet is a CONFIRM, not a build. (4) There is NO transactional email infrastructure at all — no vendor, no dependency, no mailer module. Hence the decision this card takes: mint a COPYABLE LINK the counsellor sends themselves, rather than adopt an email vendor for one slice. Acceptance, team invitations, and the personal-case collision are all explicitly out.
cards.badge: Ready. Carved 2026-08-23 after Stage 4's exit gate (MV-191) passed and MV-192 merged. THE TRAP THIS CARD IS MOSTLY ABOUT: `token_hash` is named that for a reason — the security value of the whole design is that a database reader (a compromised backup, an over-broad service-role query, a future audit export) CANNOT MINT A WORKING LINK. Storing the plaintext token in the row, logging it, returning it from a list endpoint, or putting it in an audit payload would pass every functional test and destroy the property, so criterion 3 is a test that goes looking for the plaintext where it must not be — write it FIRST. Second trap: a denial-only suite passes IDENTICALLY against a missing policy, so every policy relied on must be MUTATED, the mutants must WIDEN (a drop-mutant leaves every denial green), and the failing test NAMES read — MV-191's supabase/rehearsal/MV-191-mutation.sql is the worked example and the format to copy. Third: on this CRLF tree a source scan that splits on "\n" matches ZERO lines and goes VACUOUSLY TRUE, which is exactly how a secrecy test stops testing. NAMED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT SOLVED: a self-serve student already has a PERSONAL case from 20260802120000, so accepting a consultancy invitation would link one human to a second case — Stage 5's "without duplication" bullet. This card's only obligation is to not foreclose any answer: do not merge cases, do not block minting when the email matches an existing account, and assume one-case-per-human NOWHERE. Replaces the honest placeholder in components/workspace/case-invite-block.tsx, which today says "Sending the invitation isn't built yet." Slices 2-5 (acceptance; linking without duplication; student-visible vs consultancy-only fields; the Stage 5 exit gate) are named on the dossier but NOT carved.
